nodes.description: Whether a measured amount includes use of IMF credit.
nodes.name: includes IMF credit

nodes.description: What an economic unit has left from what it earns once what it pays out or uses is taken away, such as primary income, disposable income or saving.
nodes.name: income balance

nodes.description: Whether a claim's interest rate moves with a reference market rate.
nodes.name: interest rate variability

nodes.description: The three-letter alphabetic code ISO 4217 assigns to a currency, for example USD.
nodes.name: ISO 4217 currency code

nodes.description: The three-digit numeric code ISO 4217 assigns to a currency, for example 840.
nodes.name: ISO 4217 currency number

nodes.description: The code a country, area or region carries in the United Nations M49 standard of country or area codes.
nodes.name: M49 code

nodes.description: How long a claim runs before repayment falls due.
nodes.name: maturity band

nodes.description: A possible value of the statType property of a StatisticalVariable. Indicates that the variable reports the raw recorded values of observations.
Provides additional information on the measurement reported by a StatisticalVariable. For example, a variable measuring the price of goods may use the qualifier 'nominal'.

A place this is the national currency of: the currency its own central bank issues, or its currency union's, or, where it issues none, the foreign currency it has adopted instead. A place has exactly one; a currency that only circulates there alongside it does not count.
nodes.name: national currency of

nodes.description: What is subtracted when an amount is measured on a net basis.
nodes.name: net of

nodes.description: How offsetting amounts affect the calculation of a measured amount.
nodes.name: netting basis

nodes.description: How far an economy's production is above or below its potential: value added as recorded less the same value added cyclically adjusted. Output here means value added, as in GDP, not the gross output of production. It is negative when the economy produces below its potential.
nodes.name: output gap

nodes.description: Date for which the current data import holds only part of the source's data.
nodes.name: partial observation date

nodes.description: The policy aim a financing activity is meant to advance, separate from the purpose it serves. Each policy area narrows it with a property of its own.
nodes.name: policy objective

nodes.description: How the claims in a position are valued: by what is owed under their terms, by what they would sell for, or by what their future payments are worth today.
nodes.name: position valuation

nodes.description: What an economic unit receives from production and from owning assets, less the same kinds of income it pays out, before taxes on income and other transfers. For government, this includes taxes on production and imports less subsidies. For all resident units of an economy, this is national income.
nodes.name: primary income

nodes.description: Whether the value of output behind an amount includes taxes on products, such as VAT, import duties and excise duties, less subsidies on products. Buyers pay these taxes; producers pass them on to government rather than keeping them.
nodes.name: product tax basis

nodes.description: The part of an economic unit's disposable income, adjusted for the change in pension entitlements, that is not spent on final consumption. It is negative when final consumption exceeds that income.
An ontology property or value, together with everything below it in the hierarchy, whose data the skill explains how to interpret.
nodes.name: skill applies to

nodes.description: The provenance of a dataset whose series the skill explains how to use.
nodes.name: skill applies to provenance

nodes.description: The indicator code a statistical variable carries in its source dataset.
nodes.name: source indicator code

nodes.description: The value of the output of production less the value of the intermediate consumption it uses up: the balancing item of the production account.
nodes.name: value added

nodes.description: The code a concept carries in World Bank statistics, usually one segment of an indicator code.
nodes.name: World Bank code

nodes.description: The code an entity carries in the counterpart-area list the World Bank uses in International Debt Statistics, naming the creditor a debt is owed to.
nodes.name: World Bank counterpart code

nodes.description: The code an economy or aggregate carries in the World Bank's country and lending groups list, used across its databases.
nodes.name: World Bank economy code
